channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Romania Braces for Turmoil With Prime Minister Set to Lose Vote
item.description: Romania’s months-long political crisis is headed into unchartered territory on Wednesday as lawmakers are set to reject another candidate for a prime minister.
item.dc:creator: Andra Timu and Irina Vilcu

item.title: UNC Says Pyongyang Violated Armistice as Landmine Spat Deepens
item.description: United Nations Command said that Pyongyang violated the armistice with South Korea after investigators found an active North Korean landmine south of the inter-Korean border, a conclusion that will likely bolster Seoul’s calls for an apology over recent explosions that seriously injured its soldiers.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Trump Backs Independent AI Audits in Shift of Safety Posture
item.description: President Donald Trump endorsed using outside auditors to assess the safety of artificial intelligence systems through an accord with Silicon Valley leaders that seeks to sidestep new government rules in addressing a groundswell of concern over AI risks.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: AI Safety Debate Deepens as Trump Backs Self-Regulation
item.description: Bloomberg's Michael Shepard discusses the deepening debate over AI safety following an essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urging slower model rollouts. Shepard explains why President Donald Trump for now is rejecting strict guardrails, pushing instead for industry self-regulation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump & Tech Leaders Signed AI Agreement That Is ‘Morally Binding'
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY) says artificial intelligence will likely require a mix of industry self-regulation and protections for users, but argues Congress is moving too quickly toward new mandates. Florida Democratic Senate nominee and State Representative Angie Nixon says she doesn't agree with every position taken by the Democratic Socialists of America - or by the Democratic Party - as she makes the case for a broader coalition in her race against Republican Sen. Ashley Moody. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Leaders Agree AI Is Risky, Has to Be Safe
item.description: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang, Meta Platforms Inc. CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk talk about working together to make sure AI is safe after meeting with President Donald Trump at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Florida Senate Nominee Nixon Draws Lines With DSA, Dems
item.description: Florida Democratic Senate nominee and State Representative Angie Nixon says she doesn't agree with every position taken by the Democratic Socialists of America - or by the Democratic Party - as she makes the case for a broader coalition in her race against Republican Sen. Ashley Moody. Nixon also calls for guardrails around artificial intelligence, citing concerns about jobs, data privacy, safety and the impact of AI infrastructure on utility costs. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Paul: 'Too Soon' for 'Crazy' AI Regulation
item.description: As the White House brings AI industry leaders together in Washington, Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY) says artificial intelligence will likely require a mix of industry self-regulation and protections for users, but argues Congress is moving too quickly toward new mandates. Sen. Paul also discusses rising government debt and his objections to parts of a bipartisan bill targeting Chinese vehicles and components. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: OpenAI Dev Day (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
OpenAI has unveiled an always-on artificial intelligent agent that’s designed to proactively tackle work on a user’s behalf, competing with firms like Meta Platforms Inc. in a growing field for AI-powered digital assistants. The product, called Dots, is capable of using a computer and pulling information from various connected applications to conduct research, draft documents and develop software, OpenAI said on Tuesday.
On today's episode:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman & Ed Ludlow, Host of Bloomberg Tech Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Ann Miletti, Head of Equity Investments at Allspring Global Investments Ian Rogers, Chief Human Agency Officer at Ledger (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Trade & OpenAI Developer Day
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Bloom Energy CEO KR Sridhar, Alaska Air Group CEO Ben Minicucci, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar, MongoDB Interim President & CEO Dev Ittycheria, Institute of International Finance CEO Tim Adams, BMO Head of US Commercial Bank Tony Sciarrino, & Brinker International CEO & President Kevin Hochman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IIF CEO on Rising Rates, Emerging Markets and Tariffs
item.description: Tim Adams, CEO of the Institute of International Finance discusses rising long-term interest rates and government debt sustainability. He says higher inflation has helped keep debt ratios looking stable by masking underlying vulnerabilities, but warns that as benchmark rates rise, interest expenses are set to surge. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Boeing Beats Northrop for Navy Jet Contract to Replace F-18
item.description: Boeing Co. beat Northrop Grumman Corp to produce the Navy’s next Top Gun fighter jet, the stealthy and still classified F/A-XX, the Pentagon announced Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Trump to Tout $54 Billion Korean LNG Plan in Battleground Alaska
item.description: President Donald Trump is set to unveil South Korea’s plan to invest some $200 billion in the US, including $54 billion for a long-stalled venture to export natural gas from Alaska that’s been championed by a Republican senator in a tight reelection contest.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Ruth Liao

item.title: The Iran Standoff Is Far From Settled
item.description: The US rejected Iran’s latest proposal for a deal, with both sides believing they have leverage. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Marc Champion examines the standoff and why it remains unclear who has overplayed their hand. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NYC Pied-a-Terre Tax Rollout Blocked Again by State Judge
item.description: New York’s pied-a-terre tax rollout was blocked for a second time by a Staten Island judge who said the city improperly published property information and wrongly required homeowners to apply for exemptions.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Supreme Court Lets Trump’s Third-Country Deportations Resume
item.description: The US Supreme Court for now let the Trump administration resume deporting undocumented people to countries other than their own with little if any notice. The court will hear arguments on the issue in December.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Hegseth to Cut Pentagon Posts Held for Generals, Admirals
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth plans to cut the number of senior positions reserved for generals and admirals by 20%, a Pentagon official said.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride

item.title: Trump Loses Bid to Pause Judge’s Sanctions in IRS Case Fight
item.description: A US appeals court has refused to halt a Florida federal judge’s decision to penalize President Donald Trump and his lawyers for “bad faith” conduct in his $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service while he appeals.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Trump Spurns AI Rules, Opts for Voluntary Audits After CEO Lunch
item.description: President Donald Trump shot down the idea of new federal regulations on artificial intelligence after meeting at the White House with top industry executives amid growing global concerns over threats posed by the technology.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland, Skylar Woodhouse and Josh Wingrove

item.title: China Says Japan Ties Need ‘Normalization’ Again Over Taiwan
item.description: China’s top diplomat suggested relations with Japan had deteriorated to a low point unseen in decades, adding pressure on Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to amend her Taiwan remarks.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
